messages:
maria: quick sync — want to scope an RFC for the client SDK surface: retries/backoff + streaming ergonomics. customer asks piling up and we need a single source of truth.

cheng: +1. we've got multiple PRDs referencing slightly different behaviors. real quick: do we treat streaming failures as per-request vs per-chunk?

maria: per-request by default for simplicity, but we should define hooks for per-chunk resume if the runtime supports it. customers asked for resumable streaming for long outputs.

sam: ergonomics goals from devex side: 1) simple default that "just works" (no config) 2) explicit hooks for advanced use (backoff policy, retry predicates, streaming resume callbacks) 3) clear observable signals (events + metrics)

nate: runtime constraints: resumable streaming requires the model variant to be idempotent and the server to keep KV cache or support prefix continuation. We can expose a resume_token if the runtime persists state for X minutes.

olivia: acceptance criteria suggested from product: - API with 2 levels: simple streaming client (Stream.create(...)) + advanced StreamController. - defaults: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries, 10s initial backoff, overall deadline enforced. - streaming resume enabled only when model pinned and runtime supports resume_token.

cheng: notes on edge cases: - partial tokens duplicated on retry (client should be able to de-duplicate on application side if necessary). - network flaps causing many short reconnects -> circuit-breaker recommended. - user-supplied callbacks must not block event loop.

sam: prototype surface idea (pseudo):
```js
// simple: one-liner streaming that returns async iterator
const stream = client.streamGenerate({model: 'rwkv-xx', prompt});
for await (const chunk of stream) { render(chunk.text) }

// advanced: controller with hooks
const ctl = client.streamController({model});
ctl.on('chunk', (c) => {});
ctl.on('retry', (meta) => {});
ctl.start(prompt);
```

maria: nice. need to call out: default behavior on an unrecoverable server error -> fallback to smaller model variant if configured. that's part of the production rollout criteria.

nate: runtime will expose a compatible fallback API: /v1/streams?fallback_model=... We'll need to document latency/regression tradeoffs.

olivia: launch criteria we want in the PRD before eng-signoff: 1) API spec + migration guide 2) SDK impl in main JS package + 1 other language (python) 3) E2E test that simulates retry + resume scenarios 4) perf budget: median streaming latency < 150ms token emit (for hosted tier) 5) metrics: retries_count, resume_success, abort_rate

cheng: implementation questions: should retry predicate be pluggable? e.g., retry on 429/5xx/idempotent-error. I'd prefer default predicate but pluggable function param.

sam: agree — default predicate plus onRetry hook. Also provide a way to opt out entirely (no retries).

maria: customer stories to validate with: - AI assistant that streams long summaries (needs resume on client reconnect) - interactive chat where small transient errors should not break UX (wants fast retries) - regulated customers who want deterministic behavior (no automatic fallback to different model unless explicitly allowed)

olivia: add acceptance criteria for enterprise: admin toggle to disable auto-fallback, and audit log entries for every retry/fallback event for compliance.

nate: one more edge case: resumed stream after a long gap might hit a new model version. we need version pin info in resume_token and reject resume if model_version != pinned_version. include this in spec.

cheng: will draft RFC outline: 1) motivation & customer asks 2) API surfaces (simple vs advanced) 3) defaults (backoff params, retries, deadline) 4) resume_token format + invalidation rules 5) metrics + telemetry 6) security/compliance notes 7) tests & rollout plan 8) migration guide

sam: I'll add DevEx examples and a tiny cookbook for common patterns (no retry, optimistic local concat, resume + dedupe).

maria: timeline: draft RFC by end of week, internal review early next week, aim to land JS + Python SDK changes in sprint after. Can we make the RFC include acceptance test cases?

cheng: yes. I'll include explicit test vectors: simulate duplicated chunks, simulate transient 502s, simulate resume token expiration, simulate fallback model swap.

ci-bot: pipeline status: "build/devex-sdk" passing on main. no blockers for writing examples. :white_check_mark:

olivia: sounds good. if no objections I'll file a PR with the outline and link to this thread.

maria: go ahead. tagging @cheng to own the RFC and @sam to own examples. thanks all :thumbsup:

cheng: ack. starting draft.
